summary: Fine-tuning makes sense when you need to change a model's behavior, style, or format consistently, or when you must bake in domain knowledge or reduce latency/cost by distilling a smaller specialized model. RAG is the better choice when you need to inject fresh or frequently-changing factual knowledge, while prompt engineering should always be tried first for quick behavioral steering without training cost. In practice, teams often combine fine-tuning for behavior/format with RAG for up-to-date facts.
when_to_fine_tune: Choose fine-tuning when you need a consistent output style, tone, or structured format that prompting alone cannot reliably enforce across many requests.
Choose fine-tuning to distill a large model's capability into a smaller, cheaper, lower-latency model for high-volume production workloads.
Choose fine-tuning for deep domain adaptation (legal, medical, code) where specialized vocabulary and reasoning patterns must be internalized rather than retrieved.
Prefer RAG over fine-tuning when the underlying knowledge changes frequently, needs citations, or must be updated without retraining.

tools.best_for: Enterprise domain adaptation inside the AWS ecosystem

tools.name: Google Vertex AI Tuning
tools.pricing_paid: Pay per node-hour for tuning jobs plus per-token or per-hour serving costs
tools.best_for: Enterprise instruction tuning and distillation on Google Cloud

tools.name: Unsloth
